importance_detail.rationale: The National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act of 2026 reauthorizes and expands federal quantum information science, engineering, and technology programs across multiple agencies (NIST, NSF, NASA, DOE, etc.), authorizes specific funding amounts such as $85 million annually for NIST and $25 million annually for NASA, establishes new centers, testbeds, and workforce hubs, terminates the National Nanotechnology Program, and sets new research security and international cooperation strategies.

label: S. 3597

latest_action.text: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act of 2026 reauthorizes and updates federal programs supporting quantum information science, engineering, and technology. It extends federal initiatives through 2034, expands coordination across additional government agencies, establishes new research centers and workforce development hubs, integrates NASA into quantum activities, and terminates the National Nanotechnology Program.

affected_groups.effect: Higher education institutions and nonprofit research organizations gain access to new grant programs, traineeships, fellowships, and upgraded research facilities, while facing strict research security requirements and prohibitions involving foreign countries of concern.

Students pursuing STEM and quantum-related disciplines benefit from expanded scholarships, traineeships, research experiences, and workforce pathways, while K-12 educators gain professional learning opportunities.
Industry participants, startups, and small businesses are integrated into consortia, prize competitions, and testbeds to accelerate commercial quantum applications and supply chain development.
Agencies such as NIST, NSF, NASA, and the Department of Energy receive expanded authorities, coordination mandates, and reporting duties to advance quantum technologies and map supply chains.
Entities tied to the National Nanotechnology Program face the termination and wind-down of the program within 180 days of enactment, with provisions intended to minimize disruption to facilities.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes and updates the National Quantum Initiative Act through December 30, 2034, and adds new interagency participants such as the Departments of Health and Human Services, State, and Homeland Security.

Authorizes up to $85,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to carry out quantum standards, supply chain mapping, post-quantum cryptography deployment, and grants.
Authorizes NIST to establish between 1 and 3 Quantum Centers with up to $18,000,000 allocated per center for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
Requires the National Science Foundation to establish a Quantum Reskilling, Education, and Workforce (QREW) Coordination Hub and competitive quantum testbeds.

Adds a new title authorizing the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) to conduct quantum research and initiatives, allocating up to $25,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
Terminates and winds down the National Nanotechnology Program and the authorities of the 21st Century Nanotechnology Research and Development Act within 180 days of enactment.
Implements strict research security prohibitions and screening requirements regarding foreign countries of entity concern, foreign entities of concern, and Confucius Institutes.
missing_information: Total aggregate federal costs beyond specific authorizations allocated for NIST and NASA.
Exact implementation timelines for agency-specific grant applications beyond general deadlines.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act of 2026 reauthorizes and updates federal programs supporting quantum information science, engineering, and technology. It extends federal initiatives through 2034, expands coordination across additional government agencies, establishes new research centers and workforce development hubs, integrates NASA into quantum activities, and terminates the National Nanotechnology Program.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation represents a sweeping federal commitment to advancing quantum technology, research security, and workforce pipelines by reauthorizing core programs for nearly a decade, integrating NASA, creating new specialized centers and testbeds, and restructuring federal focus by terminating the older National Nanotechnology Program.
